label: prop:prolonged-periods-fixed-depth
title: A fixed-depth recurrence for the prolonged periods exists (Cayley–Hamilton)
html:
The prolonged Seiberg--Witten periods a_D^{(n)} = \varphi(M^n v_0) are orbits of the jet-prolongation operator M (prop:mi-sw-abelianisation) acting on the Gauss--Manin period space V of the SW family over Bring's surface. Since V is finite-rank — it is the de Rham cohomology of the family, \dim V \leq 2g = 8 for the genus-4 Bring curve — the operator M satisfies its characteristic polynomial (Cayley--Hamilton): M^d = \sum_{j<d} c_j\,M^j with d \leq \mathrm{rank}\, V and c_j the characteristic-polynomial coefficients. Therefore the operator powers — and hence the periods — satisfy the depth-d linear recurrence

M^{\,n+d} = \sum_{j<d} c_j\,M^{\,n+j},
\qquad
a_D^{(n+d)} = \sum_{j<d} c_j\,a_D^{(n+j)},

with n-independent kernel c, for every n.

This proves the existence half of conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol: a fixed-depth recurrence on the prolonged periods necessarily exists, with depth bounded by the rank of the Gauss--Manin local system. What remains is the identification half — that d and the kernel c are exactly the Bring Picard--Fuchs operator (so the kernel is the prolongation symbol, not a generic recurrence). That is fixed by computing the SW connection's local monodromy at the branch points and matching it against the residue weights a_D^{(n)} — a consistency test that requires the per-knot weights at n = 2, 3.
